definition: Present in large amounts; more than enough.
example: Fresh figs are abundant at the farmers' market in late summer.
nuance: Abundant suggests a supply that is large or even overflowing, while ample means only that there is enough for the need.
prompt: A hiker describes a forest trail after a very rainy spring.
options: Wild mushrooms were abundant along the trail after weeks of rain.
Water was so abundant on the hike that everyone rationed each tiny sip.
The trail was abundant, and weeds had covered it since no one walked there.
A single abundant pinecone lay in the middle of the path.
reasons: Many mushrooms springing up after steady rain is a clear case of a plentiful supply.
People ration water when it is running short, not when there is plenty.
This confuses the word with the look-alike abandoned, which means deserted.
One object cannot be plentiful; the word describes a large quantity.

practice.prompt: A farmer reports on this year's apple harvest.
options: The farmer felt abundant about the sunny forecast and smiled at breakfast all week.
Apples were abundant this year, so stores could barely find any to sell.
The harvest was so abundant that the farmer gave extra crates to neighbors.
The harvest was abundant, with only three apples on each tree.
reasons: The word describes amounts of things, not a hopeful or cheerful mood.
Fruit that is hard to find is scarce, which contradicts a large supply.
Having so many apples that some can be given away shows a supply beyond what is needed.
A few apples per tree is a poor yield, the opposite of a plentiful one.
